topicName: Advanced Troubleshooting, Debug Logging, and Workflow Diagnostics
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Troubleshooting, Debug Logging, and Workflow Diagnostics in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Building robust CI/CD pipelines requires deep visibility into execution flow, state, and environment variables. When workflows fail unpredictably, standard logs often do not provide enough context. This tutorial covers advanced diagnostic techniques, enabling secret-safe debug logging, self-hosted runner inspection, and systematic workflow troubleshooting."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Enabling Step and Runner Debug Logging"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitHub Actions supports verbose diagnostic logging via repository secrets. By setting specific secrets to 'true', you instruct the runner to output detailed internal execution steps."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ACTIONS_RUNNER_DEBUG: Set to true to enable diagnostic logging for the runner application itself, detailing runner communication, task dispatching, and environment setup."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG: Set to true to enable verbose logging for individual steps, often outputting internal tool commands and extensive execution traces."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"name: Diagnostic Workflow
on: [push]
jobs:
  debug_job:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Diagnostic Command
        run: |
          echo "Current Directory: $PWD"
          env
        env:
          ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG: true"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Creating Custom Diagnostic Outputs via Workflow Commands"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can programmatically control the GitHub Actions UI from within your steps by printing specific command strings to stdout. This allows you to group related logs or flag warnings conditionally."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"name: Custom Logs
on: [workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  log_control:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Group Log Output
        run: |
          echo "::group::Database Setup Logs"
          echo "Initializing migration scripts..."
          echo "Applying schema updates..."
          echo "::endgroup::"
      - name: Emit Warning
        run: echo "::warning file=app.js,line=10::Deprecation warning detected in dependency.""},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Inspecting Artifacts and State During Failures"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a test suite or build fails, retaining ephemeral build artifacts is crucial. You can use conditional execution clauses like 'if: failure()' to upload logs, core dumps, or test reports even when a preceding step aborts."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"name: Capture Failure State
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Complex Tests
        run: npm test
      - name: Upload Logs on Failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: failure-logs
          path: ~/.npm/_logs/"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Advanced SSH Debugging with tmate"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"For deeply elusive bugs that cannot be replicated locally, interactive debugging via SSH directly on the GitHub Actions runner is an invaluable technique. Third-party actions like 'mxschmitt/action-tmate' open an interactive shell session."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"name: Interactive Debug Session
on: [workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  debug_runner:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup tmate session
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering these advanced diagnostic options—ranging from secret-enabled verbose runner logs and custom console grouping to post-failure artifact collection and live SSH sessions—you can significantly reduce Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) for complex CI/CD pipeline failures."}]
